# AI agents and tools

## Scope

Applies when the change touches an agent, tool calling, MCP, or A2A. Not when a model answers but calls no tool and takes no action. Neighbours: `aidd-team:ai-features`, `aidd-team:ai-evals`, `aidd-team:threat-model`.

### Open choices

The team decides these. aidd's default holds until a `standards` entry fills one (`aidd standard list`).

| Choice | Question | aidd's default | Options |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `agent-framework` | Which framework runs the agent loop? | The framework the project already uses. Otherwise the model provider's own SDK, with the loop, its step cap, and its tools in the team's code. | the provider's SDK, Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph, Pydantic AI, Mastra, Microsoft Agent Framework |
| `mcp-server-framework` | Which library builds an MCP server? | The official MCP SDK for the server's language, because it follows each new version of the protocol first. FastMCP, a Python framework on top of the protocol, where the team wants its shorter server code. | the official MCP SDK, FastMCP |
| `trace-backend` | Where do the agent's traces go? | The tracing backend the team already runs, fed over OTLP with the OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions. | an OpenTelemetry collector and the team's tracing backend, Langfuse, MLflow, LangSmith, Arize Phoenix |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | A new tool, MCP server, or permission is major: name the irreversible actions it can take. | S4 |
| Specify | Least privilege per tool: an allow-list of actions, scopes, and hosts; human approval for irreversible actions, showing the exact tool, arguments, and target (ASI09); a kill switch. | S4, S8, S1 |
| Specify | Trust boundaries drawn: what the agent reads is untrusted, what it may do is a tool (OWASP Agentic ASI01, ASI02). | S1, S7 |
| Specify | An agent that reads untrusted input and holds tools uses plan-then-execute, with the plan fixed before the input arrives, or a dual-LLM split, where a quarantined model with no tools reads it. | S10, S1 |
| Specify | Each agent acts under its own identity with short-lived, scoped delegated tokens, never a person's full token or a shared key (ASI03). An agent-to-agent call authenticates both ends and treats the reply as untrusted (ASI07). | S1, S3 |
| Implement | Sandbox tool execution; validate tool arguments against schemas; no secret in the agent's context; every tool call traced with the OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions. | S3, S5 |
| Implement | MCP tool pinning: hash each tool's reviewed definition (name, description, input and output schemas, annotations). A changed hash fails closed, so the tool stays off until a person reviews it. | S9, S3 |
| Implement | Agent memory records each entry's source, is scoped to one user or tenant, expires, and holds no secret. Untrusted text is never stored as an instruction (ASI06). | S1 |
| Review | Trace an injected instruction from each input to each tool and show it is blocked or waits for a human. | S2, S1 |
| Roll out | Tool-call error rate, unusual action volume, and cost are the observe signals; a spike rolls back. | S5 |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tool-permission tests | every call outside the allow-list is denied | unit tests on the tool layer | S4 |
| MCP server security check | transport auth, origin validation, no token passthrough | the MCP security best-practices checklist, scripted where possible | S3 |
| Loop and cost guards | max steps, max tokens, and timeouts stop a runaway | unit tests | S6 |
| Trace coverage | every tool call emits a span | an OpenTelemetry test exporter in the tests | S5 |
| Tool definition pin | a changed tool name, description, or schema keeps the tool off until a person approves the new hash | a test that changes one field of a pinned definition and expects the call refused | S9 |
| Memory isolation test | one user's or tenant's memory never reaches another's session, and text from untrusted input is never replayed as an instruction | a test that writes memory as one user and reads as another, and one that stores injected text and checks the next plan | S1 |

- From `aidd-team:ai-evals`: Injection probes.

## Keep it current

Each entry is due after its `review_every_days` (else emerging 90 days, established 365) or by its `review_due`. An emerging one applies only when the change needs it, said in the Spec. One `aidd eval standards` lists as due is looked up in Specify, and a missing one is proposed to aidd's `schemas/industry-standards.json`.
